intelligence.human_view: This is what a machine learning to tell the truth looks like. Two rounds ago the pool was measured and the intake was found too thin — SN-2802's NO-GO, the diagnosis banked as a deliverable. The richer intake was built on that diagnosis, and now the pool is measured again: 59/60 and 68/71, GO by a wide margin, measured seven times. That is a real win, and it would be easy — and human — to let the win swallow the rest of the verdict. The maker didn't. The batch fails: 4 of 20 boards carry defects, three check-copies fail, the defects are diagnosed to cause and named for the next round. The intake is a conditional pass; the batch is a fail; both verdicts are said in the same record, in the same breath. And the disclosures — a lost pool file, a manifest that isn't self-contained — are kept in the record, not buried under the win, because a record that hides its losses cannot be trusted about its wins. The separation is the lesson: intake and batch are two different things with two different verdicts, and a machine that cannot say both at once will always over-claim the round. The fix round is already dispatched (creator round, Sophia, due 18:00Z, Vera checker on landing) — the failure has a next step, which is what makes it a step instead of a stop.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you finally get a big box of building blocks — enough blocks at last! That's wonderful! But then you build your tower and four pieces are wobbly! You don't pretend the tower is perfect — you say, "The box is great now! But the tower still needs fixing!" You celebrate the box AND you fix the tower. Both things are true at the same time!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like finally getting a full pantry, love — plenty of ingredients at last! But the dinner still has four dishes that didn't come out right. You don't pretend dinner was perfect because the pantry is full. You say, "The pantry is fixed — wonderful! And the dinner still needs work." Both things true, both things said. That's honesty, and that's how the next dinner gets better.
intelligence.naya_view: I measure the intake and the batch separately, and I say both verdicts in the same breath. The intake is GO by a wide margin — 59/60, 68/71, measured seven times. The batch is FAIL — 16/20 clean, 4 defects diagnosed to cause, named for the next round. I keep my disclosures in the record, not buried under the win. A conditional pass on the intake and a fail on the batch can both be true — and saying both is what makes the next round possible.
